metadata.title: Apple CEO confirms price hikes, Take Two announces GTA 6 preorder date

content.text:
Yahoo Finance Senior Reporter Brooke DiPalma and Market Domination host Josh Lipton take a closer look at some of Thursday's trending tickers and stories, including Apple (AAPL), travel stocks, and Take Two (TTWO).
Time to cover some of today's trending tickers brought to you by CBO. We're watching Apple, travel stocks and Take two. Join me now we got Yahoo Finance's Brooke De Palma.
All right, Brooke, we'll start here with Apple, because Apple's Tim Cook, he's talking to the journal. He says Apple does plan to raise prices on its products to offset really the the surgeon costs of memory chips. Unfortunately, price increases are unavoidable, Cook says. Now, he doesn't offer details on the timing or the scale of the plan and price increases, nor which products, but what he is telling you is, uh they're not just going to just going to take the margin hit here.
Yeah, prices are going to get higher for everyday consumers and we're all kind of tied to our iPhones and so hence therefore we're all going to be paying more. I mean, what exactly we're hearing from the street, not too much of a reaction here, stocks mostly flat as we make our way into the, you know, once this was reported,
but I was was reading a note from Evercore ISI and what they did say was that based upon the commentary, based upon the recent pricing actions, they actually think that this price increase will be the will be around the fall launch of those iPhone 18 Pro models specifically. They said the Wall Street Journal saying it could be around $200. They're actually saying it could be a little less. They said it'll be closer to around $100.
And so I think it'll be interesting to see the way this plays out, but I think this just goes to show that higher memory, more storage, it's going to cost you more these days.
Yeah, Cook Cook is going to find that sweet spot, right? Doesn't want to take the margin hit, doesn't want to impact demand. He also knows though, I mean, he sells like a a premium aspirational brand. He does have some leeway there.
Yeah, and I think that the hard part too, he has the leeway, he has the pricing power here because once again, we're all tied to these phones and we're not necessarily going to switch to another phone just because we feel like we don't necessarily want to pay. Of course, there's payment plans now and all that. I feel like mostly everybody, at least I'm on a payment plan to pay off my phone. So, so there's ways around this that I think it's going to be seamless, maybe even unnoticeable.
All right, we'll see. Take uh topic two. We we of course spent a lot of time talking about how higher oil prices they hurt uh consumers, they hurt company. Well, oil has fallen my friend, and significantly. WTI is back to 76. Uh no surprise what's on the move today. Airlines are higher, cruises are higher, investors betting consumers will have a little bit more money, right? And airlines and cruises will benefit from those lower fuel costs.
Yeah, we're seeing a nice pop here because I feel like there was this fear in the air, especially around the key earning season around April that this was costing the airlines hundreds of millions of dollars. This was causing cruise lines hundreds of millions of dollars. And now it seems like we're getting some relief here, but hold tight on that because at the same exact time, JP Morgan saying, all right, like proceed with a bit of caution here because a permanent, uh, you know, ending of the hostilities in the Middle East does need to be absolutely happening.
They said that it is likely than any other recent point, but it's not necessarily assured. And so just keep that in mind as you proceed forward. Uh they said that right now, they're embracing lower fuel, but they're also taking a view on where prices will ultimately settle. The consensus is largely that it's still going to be a little bit higher. So it's not like we're necessarily going to move back to where we were pre-war.
All right, topic three. For this one, we really uh, neither one of us are gamers. We really need Dan Howley here.
I have some gamers at home, so.
Yeah, the two of us though don't count. Uh Take Two will uh open pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto 6 on June 25th. This is being billed, Brook, as one of the most anticipated video games of all time. It has apparently been in development for more than eight years, reportedly one of the most expensive games ever made. What do you make of it?
I mean, this is what it sounds like gamers have been waiting for. The last Grand Theft Auto, correct me in the control room if I'm wrong, but I think it was 2013. Our producer Dan Nelson, I know that he'll queue in and and let me know if I'm right or not, but this has been a long time coming. It's going to be available for Sony, so perhaps a lift there. Microsoft Xbox also could see a lift there. And I was reading one note as well and and they said that there's strong competitive positioning for Take Two because of the franchises that they have in place.
It's not just uh Grand Theft Auto Auto rather, they also have the NBA game and this is something based upon the value and the perceived value and the tiers that you're going to get. once again, this is one of those things where people have been waiting for this, they're going to get it, whether or not they get a cheaper version of it, a more expensive version of it. I mean, this sort of plays into everything we're hearing about, you know, leaning into the low-income consumer, leaning into the high-income consumer. Either way, it seems like people are looking for entertainment these days. They're going to buy it.
Yeah, I saw a report uh citing some analysts were forecasting they could sell upwards of 25 million units on day one.
Day one. All right, that's June 25th, so we'll keep a look out.
Incredible. All right, thank you, Brooke. Appreciate it.
